A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WUDI-Merging. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-merging experiments on vision and language tasks, together with ablations, interference analyses and computational measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds LoRA model-merging evaluations and comparative computational measurements.

M1.justification: The balanced objective, initialization, layerwise Adam updates and closed-form alternative remain unchanged. The new LoRA paragraph constructs task vectors as BiAi and explicitly applies the existing merger directly; it does not introduce a different merging algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds a four-task Qwen evaluation suite comprising MMLU, TruthfulQA, BBQ and CNN, substantially extending language-task coverage beyond the retained GLUE and instruction/math/code evaluations (Table 6). The Flan-T5 experiment reuses the eight GLUE tasks and does not itself add dataset coverage.

E2.justification: v1's computational-resource table evaluates only WUDI-Merging. v2 Table 9 adds comparisons with Ties Merging, AdaMerging and CPU/GPU closed-form variants. Comparator membership in the retained benchmark tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds LoRA-fine-tuned Flan-T5-base and Qwen-14B evaluation configurations and separate CPU/GPU measurements for the closed-form solution. These extend the experimental settings; the existing model configurations and stated Adam settings of 300 steps at learning rate 1e-5 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The computational analysis expands from WUDI's standalone resource requirements to an accuracy, runtime and memory comparison with alternatives (v2 Table 9). The balancing, convergence, task-count, regularization, interference and subspace analyses are retained. Moving appendix plots into the main text does not add new ablation evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions describe averaging over eight sampled task subsets and retain the task-count plot's error bars (v1 Figure 3b; v2 Figure 4b). No new seed counts, repeated-run disclosures, confidence intervals or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: v2 adds complete LoRA result tables: Flan-T5 averages 81.2 versus AdaMerging++'s 78.3, and Qwen averages 55.69 versus Task Arithmetic's 54.70 and Ties-Merging with DARE's 54.62. Table 9 adds comparative resource results. Retained benchmark values are unchanged. The prose incorrectly attributes Qwen's 0.99 margin to Ties-Merging; the displayed margin over that baseline is 1.07.

T1.justification: v2 adds explicit mathematical definitions for Gaussian surrogate vectors, sampled-row subsets and their ablation losses (Equations 22–25). The main assumptions, lemma, proposition, theorem and Appendix A.1 proofs are unchanged. The newly displayed ablation losses omit the squared Frobenius norm used in Equation 21, leaving their scalar-loss formulation unclear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same task-vector theory, data-free and rescaling-free merging contribution, and performance claims. The headline 10.9% and 3.3% improvements are unchanged; the added experiments support the existing generality claim.

C2.justification: v2 newly acknowledges smaller improvements with LoRA and hypothesizes that initialization noise weakens task-vector reconstruction (Section 4.2). This mechanism is proposed without a corresponding controlled test. Existing interpretations concerning language-task conflicts, input-domain overlap and regularization sensitivity remain.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the promise of forthcoming code with a repository address and a statement of availability. v2 also documents LoRA-factor conversion and specifies Gaussian sampling and row selection for the existing subspace ablation. Hardware, software and optimization disclosures are retained, while detailed LoRA training settings remain sparse.

R1.justification: The cited-work set is unchanged. Section 2 retains the same positioning relative to data-free, test-time adaptation and MoE-like merging; its wording edits do not substantively redefine novelty or relationships to prior work.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording and heading edits, expands experimental explanations, and adds acknowledgments and conference information. The overall narrative structure remains stable, with limited appendix consolidation and renumbering.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 4, 6 and 9 and reformats existing tables. The three-model plots from v1 appendix Figures 13 and 14 become main-text Figures 3 and 6, consolidating duplicate displays. Figure 1 is relocated, while the underlying retained plots remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added LoRA evaluations test previously unsupported applicability, and the comparative resource table makes efficiency claims more assessable. Code-access information and ablation details also improve documentation. These are limited gains: LoRA settings remain sparse, the new loss formulas are unclear, Qwen's improvement is attributed to the wrong baseline, and Tables 8 and 9 report inconsistent ViT-B/32 memory values of 3.03 and 4.0 GB. The established theory and earlier empirical evidence remain intact.
